newsitem.title: USA: USDA buys 4.70 mln lbs frozen beef for programs.
newsitem.headline: USDA buys 4.70 mln lbs frozen beef for programs.

text.p: The Agricultural Marketing Service of the U.S. Department of Agriculture said it bought approximately 4.70 million lbs of beef products for use in the National School Lunch Program and other federal programs.

Since May 1, when USDA announced an accelerated beef buying initiative to aid the cattle industry, the government has bought about 75 million pounds of beef products at a cost of about $70 million, the AMS said.
The latest award under Announcement LS-48, Invitation 017, will be shipped between November 13 and 26, 1996.
Details of this week's purchase are as follows:
Total purchases since the program was announced:

Winning bidders for the fine frozen ground beef were Bauer Meat Co (Ocala FL) 475,200 lbs, Emmpak Foods Inc (Milwaukee WI) 396,000 lbs, Monfort Inc (Dumas TX) 950,400 lbs, Northern States Beef (Omaha NE) 1,188,000 lbs, Service Packing Co (Joplin MO) 396,000 lbs, and Taylor Packing Co (Wyalusing PA) 435,600 lbs.
Winning bidder for the frozen beef patties with VPP was Bauer Meat Co 316,800 lbs.
Winning bidders for the frozen beef patties 100 percent beef were Bauer Meat Co 39,600 lbs, Robzens Inc (Scranton PA) 79,200 lbs and Service Packing Co 198,800 lbs.
Winning bidders for the frozen beef patties (lean) were Aksarben Foods Inc (Omaha NE) 118,800 lbs, Bauer Meat Co 39,600 lbs, and Country Platter Inc (Wichita KS) 79,200 lbs.
